dedupe_keys.name: shore power needs and co2 reductions of ships in eu ports under fueleu maritime and afir icct 2023

description: This working paper by Liudmila Osipova and Camilla Carraro of the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT, October 2023) estimates how much shore power EU ports need to meet the FuelEU Maritime regulation and the Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR), which from 2030 require container and passenger ships of 5,000 gross tonnage or more to connect to shore power in main TEN-T ports. Coverage: ships that berthed in 489 EU ports in 2019, located with the ICCT SAVE model from AIS and IHS Markit data; about 15,700 ships spent more than 2 hours at berth, demanding nearly 5.9 TWh, 70% of it in TEN-T ports; 51 ports in 15 Member States had 309 MW of shore power. Sixteen policy scenarios vary ship types, sizes, demand and port coverage. Format and access: a 17-page PDF. Licence and cost: free to read; copyright ICCT. Caveats: one base year (2019) and modelled, not metered demand; the authors find current rules cut only 24% of 4.37 Mt at-berth CO2 and that ending it would need about 2,000 MW more at average and 3,300 MW at peak demand. The port-level berth energy demands can size grid connections and flexible loads in port electricity and capacity planning models. It relates to AISHub and the Danish Maritime Authority AIS data in the catalogue.
